name: sol_ec_1
description: Cross-function/read-only reentrancy from external calls before state updates
question: The source file in `source` contains a function that makes an external call (e.g., ETH transfer, token transfer, or callback) before finalizing state updates such as balances or reserves, allowing reentrancy into a different state-reading function (including a view function) that returns stale or inconsistent data, or into another state-changing function that exploits the intermediate state, without a reentrancy guard or effects-before-interactions ordering, excluding cases where all state is fully updated before the external call or a nonReentrant modifier protects both the calling and reentered functions.
criteria: A withdraw or liquidation function calls an external contract or sends ETH via call before updating balances or debt mappings, enabling reentry into a view function like getPrice() or totalAssets() that reads the pre-update state

A function that updates reserves/pool balances performs an external token transfer or hook call before updating the reserve variables, allowing a callback to read stale reserve values via a public getter

An AMM or vault function computes and returns share price or exchange rate using state that hasn't been updated yet because an external call earlier in the same transaction can trigger a reentrant read of that state

A function calls a user-controlled external contract (e.g., ERC721/ERC777 hook, ERC20 with callback) mid-execution and only updates critical accounting state after the call returns, with no reentrancy guard applied to the getter function used elsewhere in the protocol
